name: Solitary Necrotic Nodule of the Liver

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Solitary Necrotic Nodule of the Liver

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of a solitary necrotic nodule characterized by central coagulative necrosis surrounded by fibrous capsule without evidence of malignancy or infection
Imaging studies (CT or MRI) showing a well-demarcated, hypodense hepatic lesion without vascular invasion or satellite lesions
Exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, or inflammatory hepatic lesions by clinical, laboratory, and imaging evaluation
Usually asymptomatic or mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever or malaise

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible imaging findings and exclusion of other hepatic lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily histological; imaging and clinical exclusion of other causes are essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Asymptomatic solitary hepatic lesion detected incidentally
pathognomonic.notes: Most cases are discovered incidentally during imaging for unrelated reasons
searchTerms: silent liver lump found by chance

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized right upper quadrant abdominal discomfort
pathognomonic.notes: Mild discomfort may be present in some patients

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to mild systemic inflammation

common.notes: Palpable liver enlargement may be present

occasional.symptomName: Mild elevation of liver enzymes (ALT, AST)
Mild right upper quadrant tenderness on palpation
occasional.notes: Tenderness may be elicited in some cases
searchTerms: mild tenderness in right upper abdomen

rare.notes: Very rare, usually if lesion compresses bile ducts
searchTerms: jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile

rare.symptomName: Fever spikes with chills mimicking abscess

rare.notes: Rare and usually associated with other liver pathology

laboratory: Mild transient elevation of liver transaminases (ALT, AST)
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR)
imaging: Well-circumscribed hypodense lesion on CT without enhancement
Hypointense lesion on T1-weighted MRI and hyperintense on T2-weighted MRI
No vascular invasion or satellite nodules
other: Histopathology showing central coagulative necrosis surrounded by fibrous capsule without malignant cells
Negative microbiological cultures from biopsy specimens

distinguishingFeatures: Imaging showing fluid collection with rim enhancement
Irregular lesion with arterial phase enhancement and venous washout on imaging

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of hepatic lesion
Onset of jaundice or biliary obstruction symptoms
Systemic signs of infection such as high fever and chills
references: Kawamoto S, et al. Solitary necrotic nodule of the liver: radiologic and pathologic correlation. Radiographics. 2002;22(2):387-92.
Makhlouf HR, et al. Solitary necrotic nodule of the liver: a clinicopathologic study of 17 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1999;23(8):1001-7.
Orphanet: Solitary necrotic nodule of the liver. ORPHA:100035.
